topic: Weak-first-stage robust confidence complexes for BudgetIV

open_problems.open_problem: Can the BudgetIV standardized band-cost envelope be represented by an exact nested-quota min-cost flow whose exchange cycles yield a complete finite structural partition and a certified inversion returning every interval, singleton tangency, and ray?

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV gives a sharp, possibly disconnected finite union under magnitude-count budgets, while its scalar implementation searches over a user-supplied effect domain.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.claim: Grid inversion can miss accepted components and truncate unbounded weak-IV sets; polynomial and rational structure permits exact root-based inversion for ordinary weak-IV statistics.
source_refs.author: Gustavo Schlemper, Marcelo J. Moreira

source_refs.excerpt: an executable real-closed-field quantifier-elimination, sign-determination, and root-isolation substrate
Fix the network convention end to end: choose one node-balance sign, include the correct carry terms for every layer.
Unconditional deterministic polynomial-delay generation of all vertices remains unresolved.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Schlemper and Moreira start from one rational or polynomial statistic, but BudgetIV takes a lower envelope over assignments constrained by nested quotas. The first missing step is a bijection between tier assignments and a correctly balanced laminar flow; the next is a proof that every parameter-dependent optimizer change is generated by an enumerated exchange cycle. Only after that reduction can root isolation be complete at ties, tangencies, and zero-width components. The failed RDD flow proposal documents how an incorrect balance convention destroys such a certificate, while the BackShift proposal explicitly leaves executable sign determination and root isolation open.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete exact-arithmetic algorithm with a fixed-K polynomial min-cost-flow oracle, an exhaustive exchange-cycle cell decomposition, certified boundary-root isolation and ray tests, and a theorem of equality with exhaustive semialgebraic assignment inversion on rational inputs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes omissions caused by grid inversion an inferential failure and motivates complete recovery of disconnected and unbounded sets.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak identification creates nonstandard confidence-set geometry -> finite grids omit components and rays -> exact algebraic inversion prevents those errors -> BudgetIV needs a combinatorial-algebraic certificate for its quota envelope.

method_exemplars.technique: Clear rational denominators, isolate every real boundary root, and determine acceptance signs cell by cell.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once a BudgetIV assignment is fixed, the remaining one-dimensional inversion is the same semialgebraic root-and-sign problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use capacitated min-cost flow, node potentials, reduced costs, and complementary slackness to evaluate and certify each quota optimum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A valid laminar-network encoding would turn the standardized nested-quota assignment problem into precisely this certified optimization primitive.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode tiered invalidity as magnitude-count budgets and preserve the assignment interpretation of disconnected identified-set components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the exact feasibility constraints and component labels that the flow and boundary certificate must reproduce.

open_problems.open_problem: Does projecting the exact joint Gaussian reduced-form ellipsoid through Penn et al.'s fixed nested magnitude-count budget yield a computable complex that uniformly contains the entire BudgetIV population identified set when all first stages may be arbitrarily weak?

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV identifies a possibly disconnected finite union from population covariance parameters, but its confidence construction is asymptotic under a no-measurement-error condition for exposure associations.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.claim: AR, Kleibergen, and CLR procedures are extended to independent two-sample summary-data MR with size control under weak-instrument asymptotics.
source_refs.author: Sheng Wang, Hyunseung Kang

source_refs.claim: Union confidence intervals retain coverage under an upper bound on the number of invalid instruments, but do not impose nested magnitude tiers or target simultaneous containment of an identified set.
source_refs.author: Hyunseung Kang, Youjin Lee, T. Tony Cai, Dylan S. Small

source_refs.claim: Criterion inversion provides confidence regions for entire identified sets, but not for weak Gaussian ratio geometry combined with nonconvex nested quotas.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: VIPER proves finite-sample validity for a confidence set containing the true effect when its violation vector lies in the posited set; it does not state simultaneous containment of every population-compatible effect.
source_refs.author: Gregor Steiner, Jeremie Houssineau, Mark F. J. Steel

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature supplies separate pieces: BudgetIV's nonconvex population set, weak-first-stage Gaussian testing for valid instruments, count-invalid subset unions, and general set-criterion inference. None proves the stronger event that one random complex contains every effect compatible with the same true reduced form and nested budget. The obstacle is to exchange joint ellipsoid coverage with a set-valued projection whose optimizer changes discontinuously across quota assignments, while keeping the guarantee uniform at exactly zero and local-to-zero first stages.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit random finite union of closed intervals, singleton components, and rays C_alpha with a finite-sample bound inf_P Pr_P{Theta_I(P,Gamma) ⊆ C_alpha} >= 1-alpha over all allowed first-stage vectors and budget-feasible pleiotropy patterns.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest arc from pervasive IV invalidity to interpretable budgets and a disconnected sharp identified set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Candidate instruments are often invalid -> magnitude-count budgets encode credible relaxations -> the causal-effect set can be disconnected -> uncertainty in both reduced forms requires weak-stage robust whole-set coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Project an AR-type confidence region and use quadric geometry to obtain a weak-identification-robust confidence set and boundedness classification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed object is also an exact confidence-region projection, but through a nonconvex quota restriction rather than one structural equation.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct and invert weak-IV robust statistics from paired two-sample summary associations with exposure-association uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It uses the same two-sample reduced-form inputs and arbitrary weak-stage regime required for uniform BudgetIV inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert criterion contours to form confidence regions for a population set and prove set-level coverage and convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the whole-set inferential target that pointwise weak-IV test inversion does not.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary-and-sufficient trimmed-first-stage criterion determines whether the BudgetIV confidence complex contains its positive or negative ray, including cutoff-equality cases decided by lexicographically ordered cost coefficients?

source_refs.claim: Exact Gaussian ratio inference naturally produces bounded, complement-of-interval, or unbounded sets depending on denominator information.
source_refs.author: E. C. Fieller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Weak-IV confidence sets can be infinite and take several nonstandard forms, so full inversion must recover their tails.
source_refs.author: Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV permits instruments to occupy different magnitude-count tiers and can yield disconnected feasible sets, making tail behavior assignment dependent.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.excerpt: enumerate its minimizing treatment words at equality, and thereby test feasibility, list the complete signature
moving strength thresholds, disconnected-set taxonomy, or sharp constants.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fieller and Mikusheva explain denominator-driven rays for a single weak-IV statistic, whereas BudgetIV's tail cost is an order-and-quota statistic over several standardized first stages. At generic values, the leading squared costs can be trimmed according to quota capacity; at a cutoff equality those leading terms cancel and lower-order coefficients can change the minimizing assignment. The prior multivalued-IV construction handles equality by retaining complete discrete signatures, but does not establish eventual ordering for a rational cost envelope. The first changed step is to prove that lexicographic comparison of quota-trimmed asymptotic coefficient vectors is equivalent to exact tail ordering.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided algebraic iff theorem for ray membership based on quota-trimmed coefficient vectors, with a finite lexicographic recursion for all leading-order ties and a proof that its decision equals eventual exact inversion.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents unboundedness as information conveyed by an honest weak-IV confidence set, not as a numerical defect.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A weak denominator carries little information about a causal ratio -> honest sets reveal this through infinite extent -> ordinary IV inversion classifies possible shapes -> BudgetIV needs the corresponding quota-sensitive tail criterion.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a Gaussian quadratic inequality and classify the ratio confidence set from leading coefficients and discriminants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each fixed BudgetIV assignment has a multiband version of the same denominator-driven algebraic geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Read rays and bounded components from leading polynomial behavior plus certified root-and-sign analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That tail logic transfers after replacing one test statistic by the quota-optimal lower envelope.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one prove that no almost-surely bounded BudgetIV confidence complex is uniformly honest along local Gaussian sequences in which every quota-admissible retained first stage vanishes?

source_refs.claim: A valid confidence set for an unbounded locally almost unidentified parameter must be unbounded with positive probability.
source_refs.author: Jean-Marie Dufour

source_refs.claim: Uniformly correct weak-IV inversion can produce infinite confidence sets and must remain valid over arbitrarily weak instruments.
source_refs.author: Anna Mikusheva

source_refs.excerpt: no confidence interval with diameter o_p(1) can have uniform coverage over local perturbations
an unbounded locally unidentified coefficient, not an intrinsically bounded target complier effect.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dufour treats a locally almost unidentified parameter, but a BudgetIV procedure can switch which instruments it assigns to invalidity tiers, so nonidentification must be shown uniformly over a finite union of nuisance patterns. The proximal proposal records a related nonshrinking-set conjecture, while the transported-CACE proposal explains why Dufour's infinite-diameter conclusion does not transfer to intrinsically bounded targets. Here the scalar effect is unbounded, but the missing proof must construct contiguous Gaussian reduced-form sequences with arbitrarily separated effects that remain compatible with a common nested-budget pattern after every admissible trimming choice.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A contiguity or local asymptotic minimax theorem showing that uniform 1-alpha coverage forces a positive probability of at least one unbounded component whenever quota-admissible trimmed first-stage strength tends to zero.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the canonical argument for why local nonidentification of an unbounded target forces confidence-set unboundedness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Local nonidentification erases information about an unbounded parameter -> bounded sets cannot cover observationally contiguous values -> honest procedures must sometimes be unbounded -> prove the corresponding result for a BudgetIV quota union.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct sequences converging to a common nonidentifying distribution and use coverage to force positive-probability unboundedness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Vanishing retained first stages create the same loss of information, with the added need to control every quota assignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze weak-IV test inversion uniformly across strong, local-to-zero, and unidentified regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the Gaussian weak-IV local-experiment architecture around the BudgetIV lower bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Under which separated positive-width regular-face conditions do all finite BudgetIV endpoints have a joint limit law and does the estimated complex recover the population number, pairing, and assignment labels of connected components?

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV's feasible set can be a disconnected finite union whose components correspond to different instrument-validity assignments.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.claim: Regularized support-function estimators have uniform Gaussian limits under regular affine geometry and remain consistent in nonregular cases, separating endpoint inference from set consistency.
source_refs.author: Bulat Gafarov

source_refs.claim: Nondifferentiable bound functionals need not admit locally asymptotically unbiased or quantile-unbiased regular estimators.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano, Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: Set-criterion methods establish confidence-region and convergence results without automatically recovering labels of disconnected components.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, Elie Tamer

source_refs.excerpt: Derive the local Gaussian experiment for competing tangent cones at vanishing-edge and coincident-block strata
Replace the failure-only kernel with a new calibration or correction rule for the contact-gap endpoint

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hausdorff consistency does not prevent a narrow component from disappearing, one component from splitting, or two components from merging. BudgetIV endpoints are roots of an active-assignment lower envelope and lose differentiability at tangencies, zero-width components, exchange-cycle ties, and quota-cutoff intersections. General support-function and set-inference results do not provide the simultaneous simple-root, stable-assignment, positive-separation conditions needed to match every endpoint and label. The prior tangent-cone proposal and intersection-bound review also show that a generic directional-limit or bootstrap-failure statement alone would be incremental; the new work must give an attaining regular-face theorem and sharp failure regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint asymptotic distribution for all ordered finite endpoints plus probability-one component-and-label matching under separated simple-root regular faces, paired with explicit local counterexperiments at tangencies, zero-width components, and assignment-cutoff collisions.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames inference as estimation of a population set and separates coverage of the set from convergence toward it.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification makes the target set-valued -> criterion inversion estimates the set -> global set consistency does not identify individual boundaries -> disconnected BudgetIV needs endpoint and component recovery on regular faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize an optimization-defined endpoint, derive an asymptotically linear Gaussian representation under stable geometry, and retain consistency in nonregular cases.
method_exemplars.why_closest: BudgetIV endpoints are also optimizer-defined functionals whose active constraints must remain stable for a joint limit law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional differentiability to derive nonstandard limits and valid resampling while diagnosing ordinary-bootstrap failure at ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: BudgetIV endpoint maps are piecewise root-selection maps with the same regular-versus-tied active-set divide.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local perturbations at nondifferentiable functionals to establish impossibility of regular unbiased inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Root collisions and assignment ties make the BudgetIV endpoint functional nondifferentiable and motivate the stated failure frontier.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the full weak-stage BudgetIV confidence complex exactly equivariant under every joint SNP allele recoding after sign-conjugating each within-pair covariance block, and which conclusions in the published 48 risk-factor–disease pairs are stable across prespecified budgets?

source_refs.claim: MR-Egger conclusions differed materially across SNP orientation schemes in 48 risk-factor–disease pairs, and the problem persists beyond small samples.
source_refs.author: Zhaotong Lin, Isaac Pan, Wei Pan

source_refs.claim: MR-GRIP changes the directional-pleiotropy model to make causal-effect inference independent of allele coding.
source_refs.author: Frank Dudbridge, Bethany Voller, Ruby M. Woodward, Katie L. Saxby, Timothy M. Frayling, Luke C. Pilling, Jack Bowden

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV uses magnitude constraints and returns disconnected components, suggesting but not proving finite-sample equivariance of the complete confidence topology.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.claim: Covariance-aware weak-IV tests use paired two-sample summary associations but do not analyze nested-budget topology under all SNP sign actions.
source_refs.author: Sheng Wang, Hyunseung Kang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Population magnitude budgets are invariant to simultaneous sign flips of each SNP's outcome and exposure associations, but finite-sample equivariance additionally requires transforming covariance blocks, standardized distances, flow certificates, roots, rays, and component labels consistently. Lin, Pan, and Pan establish a consequential coding pathology for MR-Egger, whereas MR-GRIP cures it under a different directional-pleiotropy model. The searched literature does not establish BudgetIV complex equivariance or use topology-preserving budget sensitivity to reassess the same 48 pairs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact group-equivariance theorem for C_alpha under all 2^p SNP sign actions, including covariance and component-label transformations, together with a prespecified 48-pair analysis reporting budget-indexed exclusion of zero, component counts, and rays.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the empirical puzzle and 48-pair design that make recoding invariance scientifically consequential.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Equivalent SNP codings should not change causal conclusions -> MR-Egger changes under recoding even in large GWAS -> 48 pairs exhibit material instability -> BudgetIV should certify exactly which conclusions and topologies are coding invariant.

method_exemplars.technique: Reparameterize directional pleiotropy so the regression criterion respects the SNP sign-action group and prove slope invariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest formal treatment of the same allele-recoding requirement, although BudgetIV uses magnitude-count restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct weak-IV inference directly from paired summary statistics and their covariance matrices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired sign action must preserve precisely this covariance-aware reduced-form sampling law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use absolute violation thresholds and count budgets to form an interpretable disconnected effect set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Absolute-magnitude restrictions are the structural reason exact BudgetIV equivariance may hold.

open_problems.open_problem: Can VIPER's exact validification be lifted to BudgetIV's nonconvex nested magnitude-count violation set so that calibration covers the whole population identified set rather than only the true causal effect?

source_refs.claim: VIPER provides exact finite-sample validity for a true effect under a user-specified violation set and practical Monte Carlo or chi-square approximations.
source_refs.author: Gregor Steiner, Jeremie Houssineau, Mark F. J. Steel

source_refs.claim: BudgetIV supplies interpretable nonconvex nested invalidity budgets and asymptotically valid confidence sets under a common MR assumption.
source_refs.author: Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Ricardo Silva, David S. Watson

source_refs.claim: Confidence regions for an entire criterion-defined identified set require a set-level target distinct from pointwise coverage of one structural parameter.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: VIPER calibrates a profiled possibility at the singleton true effect and obtains pointwise strong validity when the true violation vector lies in the posited set. Whole-set containment instead requires controlling every effect compatible with every budget-feasible violation vector at the same population reduced form, which introduces a supremum over a nonconvex quota union. Thus the first proof step that changes is the probability-integral-transform calibration itself: pointwise validification does not directly imply a simultaneous set-covering event, and the practical Monte Carlo or chi-square surrogates do not provide the desired exact quota/topology guarantee.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an exactly calibrated, finitely computable supremum functional proving inf_P Pr_P{Theta_I(P,Gamma) ⊆ C_alpha} >= 1-alpha, or a counterexample showing that pointwise VIPER validification cannot imply whole-set coverage without stricter simultaneous calibration.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly contrasts exact validification with BudgetIV's asymptotic inference and cleanly separates exact calibration from practical approximations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Invalid instruments create partial identification -> a violation set supports possibilistic profiling -> exact validification gives pointwise finite-sample coverage -> nested BudgetIV quotas raise the stronger whole-set calibration question.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate a profiled possibility function by a worst-case sampling probability over nuisance parameters to obtain finite-sample valid level sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the donor calibration mechanism, but it must be lifted from pointwise validity to simultaneous coverage over a BudgetIV identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct confidence regions for an entire criterion-minimizer set by contour inversion and set-level analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the simultaneous coverage target that distinguishes the proposed extension from VIPER's current pointwise guarantee.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent magnitude-count restrictions as a finite nonconvex union with assignment-specific interpretations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That union is the destination geometry over which any exact validification must optimize.

literature_map:
1. Penn et al. (2025, AISTATS, arXiv:2411.06913) introduce BudgetIV, giving sharp, possibly disconnected population sets under magnitude-count budgets; their inference is asymptotic under a common MR no-measurement-error condition.
2. Wang and Kang (2022, Biometrics, doi:10.1111/biom.13524) extend AR, Kleibergen, and CLR tests to independent two-sample summary-data MR under weak instruments.
3. Kang et al. (2022, Biometrics, doi:10.1111/biom.13415) obtain invalid-IV coverage by unions over candidate invalid subsets; this is count-robust rather than nested magnitude-budget inference.
4. Moreira (2003, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/1468-0262.00438) gives exact conditional weak-IV tests in Gaussian reduced-form models.
5. Mikusheva (2010, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2009.12.003) characterizes weak-IV confidence-set shapes and emphasizes that honest sets may be infinite.
6. Dufour and Taamouti (2005, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00618.x) project AR-type quadrics and derive analytic boundedness conditions.
7. Schlemper and Moreira (2026, arXiv:2604.04279) show that grid inversion misses components and rays and use polynomial roots for exact ordinary-IV inversion.
8. Dufour (1997, Econometrica, doi:10.2307/2171740) proves that valid inference near local nonidentification of an unbounded parameter cannot remain almost surely bounded; Fieller (1954, JRSSB) supplies the canonical Gaussian-ratio geometry.
9. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x) develop criterion-based inference for entire identified sets, distinct from pointwise structural-parameter coverage.
10. Beresteanu and Molinari (2008, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2008.00859.x) provide random-set consistency and inference; Gafarov (2025, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.105952) separates regular Gaussian endpoint limits from nonregular consistency.
11. Hirano and Porter (2012, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8681) show that nondifferentiable bound functionals can preclude regular unbiased inference.
12. Steiner, Houssineau, and Steel (2026, VIPER, arXiv:2511.16029) prove exact finite-sample pointwise validity under a user-specified violation set, with practical Monte Carlo and chi-square approximations, not whole-identified-set coverage.
13. Lin, Pan, and Pan (2022, PLOS Genetics, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1010166) document materially different MR-Egger conclusions across SNP recodings in 48 risk-factor–disease pairs.
14. Dudbridge et al. (2025, PLOS Genetics, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1011967) propose MR-GRIP to restore coding invariance under a directional-pleiotropy model distinct from BudgetIV.
15. The unoccupied intersection is exact weak-stage, covariance-aware, whole-set inference for nonconvex nested BudgetIV quotas with certified recovery of every finite component and ray.
